text: by Kurt Schlosser on Oct 27, 2026 at 9:03 am October 27, 2026 at 9:29 am Avante , the maker of an AI platform to help companies manage employee health care and other benefits, has landed a $30 million Series A round. Frist Cressey Ventures led the round, with participation from Sorenson Capital, Hearst Ventures, Morgan Stanley Next Level Fund and existing investor Fuse. The new funding, announced Tuesday , brings Seattle-based Avante’s total raised to $40 million, following a $10 million seed round led by Fuse in 2024. Benefits are one of employers’ biggest costs. Avante’s AI agents do work like comparing vendor contracts against actual claims, reviewing plan documents for errors and preparing for renewals. Employees can also use the platform to ask questions about their own coverage. The startup plans to use the cash to expand internationally and develop more AI agents, building on a beta release of its “Ava Agents” last week. Avante says it now has more than 70 customers, including Samsung Semiconductor, Real Chemistry, Zscaler and News Corp, and that bookings grew nearly fivefold over the past year. The platform reaches more than 385,000 employees and family members, according to the company. Avante was founded in 2023 by CEO Rohan D’Souza ; Carly Eckert , a physician and epidemiologist who serves as head of innovation and impact; and executive chairman Kabir Shahani , the co-CEO of Amperity. D’Souza and Eckert previously worked as executives at health care automation company Olive AI, which shut down in 2023. The startup emerged from stealth in early 2024 and launched publicly in April 2025. “Benefits teams are responsible for one of the largest and most consequential investments their companies make, yet they’re still operating with outdated information, archaic spreadsheets, and technology built for another era,” D’Souza said in a statement. Avante is pitching its software as employers face rising health care costs. Large employers are projecting a median 9.2% increase for 2027, the company said. The startup competes with benefits and HR software providers such as Workday, ADP, Deel and Rippling. It has also signed partnerships with benefits advisory firms including Gallagher, OneDigital, Segal Benz, Howden and USI Insurance Services. Avante ranks No. 156 on the GeekWire 200 , our list of top Pacific Northwest tech startups.
